rationale.en: If the wh-word is the subject, the verb carries the tense and no do/does/did is added; if it is the object (or an adverbial like where/when/why/how), the question inverts with do/does/did. Here the correct filler is "{answer}".
rationale.ru: Если wh-слово — подлежащее, время несёт сам глагол и do/does/did не нужен; если оно дополнение (или обстоятельство where/when/why/how), вопрос строится с инверсией и do/does/did. Здесь верный вариант — «{answer}».

contexts.stem: Who ___ you last night? (call) — I want to know which friend phoned.
Who ___ you invite to the party? (invite) — tell me the guest's name.
What ___ the accident? (cause) — the report names a single factor.
What ___ she tell you? (tell) — repeat her exact words.
Who ___ the window? (break) — somebody is clearly responsible.
What ___ yesterday? (happen) — I missed the whole thing.
Which book ___ less? (cost) — point me to the cheaper one.
Who ___ you see at the station? (see) — I think you recognised somebody.
Where ___ you go after work? (go) — you left in a hurry.
Why ___ she leave so early? (leave) — nobody explained it.
Who ___ the door? (open) — it was locked a minute ago.
What ___ you buy at the market? (buy) — show me the receipt.
Who ___ the cake? (make) — it tastes amazing.
When ___ the film start? (start) — I don't want to be late.
Which team ___ better this season? (play) — the table makes it obvious.
Whose car ___ the exit? (block) — someone needs to move it now.
How many people ___ the petition? (sign) — we need the final count.
Which of you ___ the documents? (bring) — I asked for them this morning.
Where ___ they usually travel in summer? (travel) — they're always away.
Which button ___ the machine? (stop) — I need the right one.
Who ___ this film? (see) — I want to discuss the ending with someone.
Who ___ tonight? (come) — set the table for the right number.
Which door ___? (open) — only one of them works.
Why ___ he change his mind? (change) — it surprised everyone.
How ___ they manage the budget? (manage) — their method works.
What kind of music ___ you happy? (make) — I'll put it on.
How come you ___ call me back? (negative past) — I waited all evening.
When ___ the museum close on Sundays? (close) — I might visit later.
Who ___ call first? (should) — somebody has to take the lead.
What ___ found at the scene? (be, past) — the report lists the items.
Which companies ___ fined last year? (be, past) — name them precisely.
Who ___ know the answer? (might) — I'm asking around the office.
Which employees ___ the bonus? (receive, past) — payroll has the list.
Which employees ___ the company promote? (promote) — I mean which staff management promoted.
Who ___ arrested after the protest? (be, past) — the news won't say.
Who ___ volunteer for this? (would) — we need one person.
What exactly ___ the change in policy? (prompt, past) — be specific.
Who on earth ___ this? (do, past) — the mess is unbelievable.
Which of the proposals best ___ the concern? (address) — pick one.
Who ___ have been notified first? (should) — protocol was ignored.
What ___ ultimately decided at the meeting? (be, past) — the minutes are vague.
Who ___ you think will win? (do) — the matrix clause takes the auxiliary, not 'will win'.
Who ___ what at the hearing? (say, past) — only one wh-word fronts; the verb stays plain.
Which of the many factors contributing to the crisis ___ been addressed? (have, present perfect, singular subject) — only one has.
Who ___ have foreseen this outcome? (could) — the implied answer is 'no one'.
By whom ___ the order signed? (be, past) — formal pied-piping, passive subject question.
Who ___ whom about this? (tell, past) — formal, with 'whom' as the in-situ object.
What, if anything, ___ changed since then? (have, present perfect, singular subject) — a cautious rhetorical form.
Which of us ___ without fault? (be, present, singular) — a rhetorical subject question; the answer is 'none of us'.
Who among the candidates ___ the most experience? (have, present, singular subject) — pick the strongest.
What greater honour ___ there? (be, present, singular) — an archaic rhetorical subject question.
Who ___ leaked the documents? (have, present perfect, singular subject) — the newsroom is investigating who is responsible.
What ___ caused the market crash, in the end? (have, present perfect, singular subject) — analysts still disagree.
